title: Affine space morphisms are limits of affine finite-presentation morphisms
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A space is quasi-compact if it admits a surjective etale atlas from a quasi-compact scheme, and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. A morphism is quasi-compact if its pullback along every affine scheme test has quasi-compact source, and quasi-separated if its relative diagonal is quasi-compact. An affine morphism is representable by schemes and has affine scheme source after every affine scheme test. Local finite type and local finite presentation are tested on compatible etale scheme charts [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Finite presentation means quasi-compact, quasi-separated and locally of finite presentation. Let $p:Z\to B$ be affine and assume $B$ quasi-compact and quasi-separated. There exist a small nonempty directed set $I$, an inverse system $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ over $B$ with affine transition morphisms, and compatible $B$-maps $Z\to Z_i$, such that each $Z_i\to B$ is affine and of finite presentation and $Z\cong\varprojlim_i Z_i$ as an fppf sheaf over $B$.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal A=p_*\mathcal O_Z$. The relative-Spec correspondence gives a quasi-coherent algebra $\mathcal A$ and $Z\cong\operatorname{Spec}_B(\mathcal A)$ over $B$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-algebra-fp-directed-colimit] using precisely the assumed quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of $B$. Obtain a small nonempty directed system $(\mathcal A_i)$ of finitely presented algebras with colimit $\mathcal A$.

Set $Z_i=\operatorname{Spec}_B(\mathcal A_i)$. Contravariance of the correspondence supplies the transition maps and the compatible maps $Z\to Z_i$, with their identity and composition laws. Its finite-presentation clause makes every $Z_i\to B$ affine and of finite presentation. The transitions are affine: over an affine etale chart $U\to B$, each transition is a map between the affine schemes $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A_j(U))$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A_i(U))$, hence affine by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-affine-schemes-affine]. Such charts exist by [lem-a1-space-affine-etale-cover]; their pullbacks cover $Z_i$ by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Affineness therefore descends by [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality].

On each affine etale chart $U=\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$, [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-affine-chart-calculus] identifies the given algebra colimit with $\mathcal A(U)=\varinjlim_i\mathcal A_i(U)$. The relative-Spec chart formulas identify the pulled-back cone with $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A(U))\to\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal A_i(U))$. By the affine case of [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition] this is a limit of schemes, hence also of their represented fppf sheaves: evaluation on a test scheme is exactly the scheme-limit universal property. Sheaf limits and their base changes are computed on sections, so this identifies the comparison $Z\to\varprojlim_i Z_i$ after each chart. These charts cover $B$; after pulling them back to any test scheme, their local inverse maps agree on overlaps by uniqueness and glue by the sheaf axiom. Thus the comparison is an isomorphism over $B$.

Step 1: by its statement, the relative-spec correspondence gives p_*O_Z in QCAlg(B) and Z ≅ Spec_B, and the new 082A node then applies with exactly the qcqs hypotheses on B. Step 2: contravariance of the correspondence gives the maps and their laws, and its fp-iff clause uses the same chart-wise R[T]/(f) definition, so each Z_i→B is affine and of finite presentation. Transitions are affine: pulled back to the disjoint-union atlas they are disjoint unions of affine-scheme maps (01SH), and lem-sfb-space-affine-locality's iff clause then applies. The step is slightly compressed (one chart vs a disjoint union) but the gap is elementary. Step 3: the qcoh chart calculus computes the filtered algebra colimit on charts; the chart formula and 01YW give Spec(colim) as a limit of schemes, hence of representable sheaves; the comparison is an isomorphism on each chart and glues by uniqueness and the sheaf axiom over the pulled-back fppf cover. The new node lem-sfb-space-algebra-fp-directed-colimit is statement-only and self-contained, with source Tag 082A, adequate stmt_deps and four kinds of recorded searches. It is true (Stacks 082A); I tested empty X, an already finitely presented algebra, and a polynomial algebra in infinitely many variables. It is not a duplicate: a 082A grep over the DAG finds only the integral 082C node, which needs integrality and only inlines the same construction, and the module-level and finite-type nodes. It is a genuine lemma, strictly smaller than the item, not a restated clause.
